about: GENERATED by scripts/sync-fix-checks.py from the canonical fix-checks registry (the snow goal's hidden_files/fix-checks.json) - the repo-pinned subset CI runs as the registry merge gate (issue #178). Do not hand-edit: register probes in the canonical registry, re-run the sync, and push the regenerated files in the same round.

provenance.subset_rule: v1: every target the probe names lives inside the repo tree (see sync-fix-checks.py)

checks.fix: The beta tree's CSP stamp carries https://tiles.basemaps.cartocdn.com (Beta 1.4 fix, after Andrew caught the dark basemap blocked on his phone). If this probe fails, the beta tree has regressed the host fix — restore the host in its POLICY_TEMPLATE before shipping anything built from that tree.
The beta service worker must at least parse — a syntax error in sw.js silently kills ALL offline capability while the app looks fine online (the 2026-11-01 lesson class). node --check is the floor.

Street-name labels ride the engine's tier layers: each tier carries the name field and hands over at its zoom bound (maxzoom 16.4). If labels lose their name source or handover, streets go anonymous at some zoom — restore the tier label layers. (Rolled 2026-11-20 by labelretire-1258, Beta 1.258: the pinned text was the app-title layer construction / the nudgeFifth body - both retired with the title system; this probe now pins their absence.) (Rolled 2026-11-20 by labelmix-1261, Beta 1.261: the tier title layers are restored under the zoom-15 cap; this probe pins their construction again)
The retired hand-rolled 'streetnames' layer stays OUT of the shipped styles — labels come from the protomaps tiers via the engine. Its return means an old style block crept back in.

The OTHER theme's sprites are pre-warmed through the worker at boot (Beta 1.41), so a day/night flip never waits on a cold sprite fetch. Removing the pre-warm brings back the flip flash. (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)
The splash element stays in the static markup — the launch still and the live splash are the same surface from the first frame.

REPOINTED 2026-11-14 by the splash-artwork-only round (Beta 1.191, PR #35): this probe's pattern was the splash icon TILE's radius - the only 'border-radius: 38px' in head.html lived on the old #splashIcon rule (the launch stills are PNG link tags, no CSS radius). Andrew's approved change removes the tile, so the guard flips to grep_absent: it now fails if the tile radius ever returns.
The boot gate waits for the map's intro conditions (GL ok + first tiles) or the 6 s escape before arming the route menu — the menu never arms over an unsettled first frame.
checks.pattern: if ((typeof glOk !== 'undefined' && glOk && typeof tilesOk !== 'undefined' && tilesOk > 0) || Date.now() - t0 > 6000) { clearInterval(iv); arm(); }

checks.fix: Map creation stays DEFERRED behind bootMap() (Beta 1.44 form: created when the boot tail runs, not at script eval) — an eval-time map was the splash-stutter class.

(File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)

The stale-fix watchdog restarts GPS preserving RUN OWNERSHIP (Beta 1.48 B02): it captures gpsFromRun BEFORE stopGps clears it — a mid-run restart that came back as non-run GPS silently stopped recording the run.
checks.pattern: const wasRunGps = gpsFromRun; stopGps(true); startGps(wasRunGps, true);

checks.fix: stopGps stays the one teardown that refreshes the GPS UI state with the watch (watch id, run flag, stale timer, render loop, compass). Bypassing it leaves stale chrome over a dead watch.
backupObj FAILS CLOSED: a route field whose raw read fails returns null (no export) instead of shipping a valid-looking backup with a piece silently missing (B04 discipline).
checks.pattern: const v = rawRead(key); if (v === RAW_READ_FAILED) return null;

The OLD backup filename (snow5w-backup…) stays gone from app4 — its return means the B09 rename regressed.

netFirst's first race is BOUNDED at 3.5 s before the bounded-wait fallback — an unbounded first wait hangs the app's start on a dead connection despite a cached copy. (Beta 1.221, PR #98, 2026-11-17: re-pinned - piece 6 replaced the 3.5 s race literal with the 2 s TIMEOUT race; the bound this probe guards is now 2000.)
The shell install stays inside e.waitUntil — the worker must not activate before the integrity-checked CORE is stored, or the first offline launch serves a half shell.

checks.fix: The row-cache reuse path verifies every cached row is still mounted before trusting it — a detached row painted as live is the stale-list class.

syncViewport pays for a map resize ONLY when the container actually changed size (Beta 1.50 P10) — it fires on every viewport scroll tick, and an unconditional resize per tick was pure jank. (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)
The offline download runs a bounded POOL of five workers (Beta 1.50 P07) — one-at-a-time was the slowest wait in the app; unlimited would flood the phone. Five is the measured middle.
checks.pattern: await Promise.all([preWorker(), preWorker(), preWorker(), preWorker(), preWorker()]);

checks.fix: Tile-cache eviction stays BATCHED (every 25 puts) and, since Beta 1.285 (issue #175), trims VECTOR TILES ONLY to MAX_TILES - glyphs, sprites and style JSON share the browsing cache but are never evicted (a glyph miss fails the whole tile parse). Per-put eviction thrashed the cache; no eviction silently eats the phone's storage. (Re-pinned in the offline-cluster round: the pre-1.285 pattern was the indiscriminate trim line this fix replaced.)

Viewport resync stays wired to visualViewport resize — without it the chrome anchors (--vvt/--vvh/--vvb) go stale and menus strand off-screen after keyboard/resize changes. (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)

checks.fix: The note editor is NEVER scrolled into view programmatically (scrollIntoView caused the page-pan stranding class); field visibility is ensured by the keyboard owner's local scroll/shift instead.

saveAll reports the storage-outcome contract: a failed key surfaces via storeFail(failedKey, true) so callers can warn honestly (Phase 3 form, pattern changed 2026-11-04). Never return to silent boolean saves.
Finish runs as a verified TRANSACTION (finishRun builds its step list and runs runTx) — a half-written finish was the corrupt-board class. The step-list form is the contract.

The eviction counter SEEDS from the cache's real size on the worker's first tile put after a wake (Beta 1.57): iOS kills the worker constantly, and a memory-only counter let the tile cache drift far past its cap.

The app asks the platform for persistent storage (Beta 1.57) so progress + offline maps are exempt from automatic eviction where supported. Fire-and-forget; removing it silently re-exposes Andrew's data to the 7-day tab eviction class. (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)

The document-height FLOOR stays (Beta 1.60): on iOS 26/27 a too-short document gets an undersized layout viewport (the 59pt strip). Proven on Andrew's iPhone 2026-11-01; removing it brings the strip back.

While the keyboard is up the layout variables FREEZE at their pre-keyboard values (Beta 1.61): the keyboard overlays the app instead of resizing it — the live-chase re-fit the sheets on every keyboard tick and the note menus flickered (Andrew, 2026-11-01). (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)

checks.fix: A note DRAFT is scoped to its street (noteEdFor names the editor's owner): switching streets finalizes the old editor against ITS street first — a draft landing on the wrong street is data corruption in miniature.
checks.pattern: noteEdFor names the street whose editor is actually in the DOM: the draft's owner

checks.fix: Verified writes are the rollback primitive (Phase 4, C3): txSet/txDel write AND read back, so a rollback knows the truth. An unverified rollback can 'restore' a lie.
checks.pattern: trust is earned by read-back; runTx undoes in reverse

checks.fix: Deletions REPORT like writes (Beta 1.63, F03): a failed removeItem used to be invisible, so 'deleted' state resurrected on the next load. lsDel's honesty is the contract.
pushGps stays the single sync from GPS state to the map's gps source (dot/beam/ring features rebuilt per call) — a second writer desyncs the dot from the recorded state.
The trail's session markers are RUN-SCOPED state loaded with the route's session record — markers describing another run would split this run's trail at wrong places.
checkStale stays the stale-run judge (a run left open across days gets its banner + honest state) — removing it lets a forgotten run silently absorb a new day’s work.

The loader NORMALIZES what it reads (history entries filtered to real objects, etc.) — storage is untrusted input; a loader that assigns raw stored structures lets one corrupt record poison the board. Re-pinned 2026-11-16 (Monday prune): the A-05 indexed loader pass (PR #79) replaced the filter form with the indexed predicate; the normalize-on-load claim stands.
checks.pattern: if (h && typeof h === 'object' && !Array.isArray(h) && !isNaN(Date.parse(h.at)) && h.items && typeof h.items === 'object') {

checks.fix: netFirst's wait is BOUNDED for every request class (nav 5 s, others 8 s past the first race) — a never-settling fetch used to hang a request forever despite a cached copy (Beta 1.64, F09).
stopCompass tears the compass down with its generation bump — a leaked orientation listener keeps rotating a dead map and drains battery.
The render loop stays the single frame driver for dot/camera/heading — GPS state advances only through it (plus its starvation pump).
The splash background OVERSHOOTS the screen edges (inset -70px) so no light frame can leak at the splash's edges during the handover.
The render loop has ONE declaration/start path (startRenderLoop arms requestAnimationFrame(renderLoop)) — a duplicated loop double-paints and double-consumes fixes.

GPS callbacks carry their watcher's GENERATION (Beta 1.69, N04): a queued callback from a stopped/replaced watcher is dropped even when its timestamp is fresh — the R01 guard cannot tell watchers apart.

Keyboard-settle conclusion NEEDS A REAL DROP (Beta 1.69, N02): unchanged samples alone no longer prove settle — iOS can report full height for hundreds of ms before the keyboard moves, and the old sampler lined the field up against wrong geometry, never to recheck. (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)
checks.pattern: unchanged samples do not prove settlement (iOS reports full height early)

checks.fix: The modal card's keyboard shift is measured from the UNSHIFTED rect (Beta 1.70, A02): measuring the already-shifted card replaced its shift with a smaller one and dropped the field back under a grown keyboard. (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)
checks.pattern: measure from the UNSHIFTED rect (the tracked shift added back)

checks.fix: Keyboard CLOSE waits for the height to RISE back and settle before releasing the frozen state (1.54/1.55 lifecycle): dropping it at blur re-animated the sheet 'like opening for the first time' against a moving target (Andrew, 2026-11-01). (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)

checks.fix: trailKm counts a segment only when BOTH endpoints belong to the run (Beta 1.70, A05) — one-endpoint counting credited the run with distance driven before it started.
checks.pattern: a segment counts only when BOTH endpoints belong to the run

checks.fix: The piece-time sanitizer is BOUNDED by the street's true part count — an unbounded stored array is how an injected {Velmar:[99]}-class record grows teeth.
The trail break rule (gap > 300 s, jump > 1000 m) lives in trailSegments ONLY (Phase 2) — trailKm consumes its segments; a second copy of the rule in the consumer is how the two drifted apart before.
checks.pattern: the break rule (gap > 300 s, jump > 1000 m) lives in trailSegments now

checks.fix: trailKm compares its window boundary at SECOND precision (Beta 1.71, B04): trail timestamps are whole seconds — a mid-second start otherwise discards the run's first legitimate segment.
checks.pattern: timestamps are whole seconds: compare at the same precision

checks.fix: GPX export walks the trail with the SESSION MARKERS as its segment boundaries — markers are data the export must consume, not recompute; a marker-less export merges separate cleans into one track.
drive127 steps the page's clocks DETERMINISTICALLY (50 ms steps) — the dot-smoothing checks are meaningless against a real wall clock (the drive's own lesson, Beta 1.115 era).
checks.pattern: The page's clocks are now stepped exactly, 50 ms at a time

checks.fix: The preload covers the map's MINIMUM zoom (z8 up — Beta 1.72, R04): the map allows zoom 8 but the preload stopped at z10, so offline at z8–9 the basemap had nothing to draw.

Session-marker saves are HONEST (saveSess returns the storage outcome; a failure arms the retry flag instead of claiming success) — a silently failed marker save corrupts the trail's segmentation later.
flushAux RETRIES the session markers when their save failed (sessDirty) — the retry flag is the only thing standing between a transient failure and a permanently wrong trail segmentation.

A legacy restore CLEARS the replaced trail's session markers inside the verified write set (Beta 1.73, C06): markers describe the trail being replaced and would split the restored trail at wrong places. Andrew's call; the entry is written and verified like every other. Beta 1.287 (issue #172): the clear moved into the merge plan (incoming form); the claim is unchanged.
buildGpx's marker pointer WALKS forward monotonically through the trail (Phase 2 form) — re-scanning from the top per marker is O(n²) and was the export's stall.
buildGpx's pointer RE-SEEKS (binary search back) when a session boundary moved behind it — without the re-seek a reordered trail silently mis-segments the export.

checks.fix: Night menus wear the neutral CHARCOAL card (32,33,37 at 94% — Beta 1.75, Andrew's pick sampled from a Google Maps dark reference), not the old blue-black. A palette drift here is a design regression he will see instantly.

Splash and route menu share the ONE blue — since Beta 1.174 that blue is the app icon's shaded gradient (linear-gradient(135deg, #3d65ef, #1b2fb6), re-pinned from the retired flat #2b4bf2) — the menu takes the splash's screen, so a second blue reads as a seam during the handover.

checks.fix: SUPERSEDED in Beta 1.233 (PR #113, Andrew's Package B call): the Clear tab's undo-arrow glyph was replaced by the Icons8 Dustpan glyph - Andrew chose the swap explicitly, overruling the 2026-11-01 rationale below. This probe is now a supersession guard: the old undo-arrow path must never return to parts/app4.js. Original rationale (historical): the undo-arrow read as 'take back the trail'.
Per-route storage SLOTS are derived in ONE place (routeKeys) — hand-listed keys per route are how a field gets left behind on switch/delete (the sweep-by-construction rule).
The legacy (pre-slots) route migration exists and fills ONLY empty slots — Andrew's pre-1.76 progress must survive the move, and a migration that overwrites is a wipe.

The route menu markup stays a boot-classed top-level surface in the static page (the splash borrows it at boot; the Routes tab reopens it) — moving it into JS-rendered markup breaks the first-frame contract.
The Routes tab stays in the tab bar markup — it is the door to the one route surface (Beta 1.78).
The coverage-index sanitizer runs IN THE LOADER (against the loaded route's samples) — stored coverage indexes outside the street's samples are dropped there, not trusted.

checks.fix: ONE corner-X rule styles every sheet/dialog close (Beta 1.30/1.31, completed 1.34): a plain red X, no box, top-right. The 1.34 bug was dialogs carrying their own overrides that repainted the X as a red box; a NEW menu's X joins this selector the day the menu is built.
closeSheets closes EVERY sheet by class (Beta 1.77) — no hand-kept list to fall behind a new menu; the tap-away path relies on it covering any sheet.
Auto theme is computed from real SUN MATH (sunTimes over the route position) — a hand table of sunrise hours drifts wrong within weeks.
The theme override is SESSION-scoped state (setThemeOverride) — the sun takes over again at the next boundary or full app open (Beta 1.77); persisting it made one evening tap a permanent theme.

A boot pick plays the intro flight (introToRoute: wide POI dwell, then the slow flight into the fitted view — Beta 1.77/1.81, Andrew). A switch frames instantly instead; the flight is boot choreography only. (File rolled app4.js -> app5.js in Arch-1, round-release-stamp, 2026-11-18: the guarded code moved with app4's tail split at the What's New seam; the invariant is unchanged.)

MapLibre is handed a COPY of the embedded styles, never the original (Beta 1.77): MapLibre rewrites fields of a style object it is handed — a night boot followed by a day flip rewrote the night style's own sprite and the offline preload then missed the dark sprites (893 files, not 897).
The old Routes SHEET stays retired (Beta 1.78): the full-screen route menu replaced it; a routeSheet element returning means the retired surface crept back.

The 'Currently loaded' badge's close-button suppression is TAB-mode only (#routeMenu:not(.tab) hides #rmClose's badge-era form) — at boot nothing is loaded yet, and the badge landing mid-exit read as a flicker (Andrew, live catch).
The Routes tab opens the FULL-SCREEN route menu (openRouteMenu — one route surface, Beta 1.78), not a sheet. The small Routes sheet is retired.

The route menu's close is a BARE white X at bottom centre (Beta 1.80, Andrew's pick from six rendered options) — no circle, no frosting; the 44px box is only the touch target. Re-pinned 2026-11-16 (Monday prune): the sweep re-run's E-05 fix moved the close buttons to position: fixed; literal followed, guard unchanged.
The engine reads the active route ONLY through the host (H.activeRoute — Phase 6 repoint): a direct app-global read from the engine breaks the boundary and the route POI with it.
Sheets open at HALF height (Beta 1.79, Andrew: closed / half / full stops) — max-height is half the visible viewport height. Full-height opening was the 'menu ate the map' complaint.

Sheet dragging is seamless: while dragging the transition drops and the sheet wears the SOLID card colour (Beta 1.98) — repainting a full-screen blur per frame is what made drags stutter behind the finger.

A Streets rebuild finalizes the open editor's pending save SYNCHRONOUSLY first (Beta 1.79): a debounced timer pointing at a discarded textarea stranded notes (drive88) when a style-ready refresh landed mid-edit.

Created routes live one-record-per-route in the IndexedDB database snowroute-userdata, store packs (Beta 1.166): the split of the snowroute.v2.userpacks localStorage monolith - one route's save can no longer crowd out, corrupt or block another's, and localStorage keeps no created-route geometry after migration.

Migration from the legacy monolith commits only behind this marker (Beta 1.166): every legacy route is put to the store and verified, parity is re-checked against a fresh full read, and only then is the marker written (verified) and the legacy record deleted - any failure leaves the legacy record authoritative and the migration retries next launch.

Boot fills the created-route picture from BOTH homes (Beta 1.166): the store registers fill-only, the still-standing legacy record wins per id, and userPackCache - the synchronous picture the backup builders read - is only ever updated at verified commit points, so boot never depends on a created-route write succeeding.

A created-route store write counts only when the record reads back identically (Beta 1.166): upPut verifies by read-back after the transaction commits, so a disclosed save success is a proven one and a failed write surfaces as that route's failure alone.

Every backup carries the Settings toggles (Beta 1.166): backupObj reads the settings record with the same strictness as the night pair and attaches it additively as the envelope's settings field - old backups without it leave device settings untouched, and a failed settings read fails the whole export, never a silent drop.

A restore validates the backup's settings BEFORE any write (Beta 1.166): canonicalSettings applies loadSettings' own per-field rules and refuses the restore outright on a malformed record; SETTINGS_KEY sits in the rollback scope unconditionally, so a failed restore puts the device's own toggles back.

Restore writes restored geometry into the IndexedDB store FIRST, one verified upPut per route (Beta 1.166), before the localStorage write phase - and any failure in either phase rolls back BOTH homes, so a restore stays all-or-nothing across the split storage exactly as it was across the monolith. drive156 B5/B6 hardening (PR #30, merge af7cf9fdec85; fix round drive156-b5b6, 2026-11-13): diagnosis proved a TEST synchronization defect - B5's real mouse press was fired with no wait for the sheet to be at rest after B4, so when the bar->panel morph was still in flight the press landed where the head had been (rect read mid-flight; head travels ~354 px during the flight) and the gesture was lost; B6 cascaded (Review is a no-op when the panel never collapsed). The app reached its terminal state in every instrumented capture where the gesture engaged the head. The fix: a rest wait on the app's own terminal signal (wanted face displayed, other faces gone, no morph in flight, sheet inline height cleared) before the press, and the B5/B6 outcome polls wait on that same terminal signal instead of face visibility alone. Assertions unchanged in content. Quarantine NOT lifted by the fix - that is Andrew's call on the 10-consecutive-run proof. If a probe fails, the hardening has been reverted or the B section rewritten - restore the shipped form and re-run drive156.

The stored form is the lossless 'e3' packed encoding (parts/app3.js): per-session varint byte streams (IEEE-754 bit-pattern deltas for coordinates, bit-pattern deltas for accuracy/speed/heading, micro-degree integer deltas for estimator outputs, float64-bit-pattern keyframe timestamps) packed 7 bits per character, applied only at the storage boundary; the decoder accepts BOTH the v1 array form (<= 1.189) and e3, must consume each stream exactly (header carries entry count + byte length), and non-finite leaves collapse to null exactly as v1's JSON did. fixLogTrim enforces both caps on a byte-accounted estimate (every appended entry measured through the one encoder; accounts in a WeakMap so in-memory sessions keep the 1.189 shape); a lone session is head-trimmed live or not, oldest-of-several evicted whole; the new head's accounted length is re-measured in keyframe form (never an accumulating allowance); fixLogOut re-applies the trim after growing an entry's account. canonicalFixLog applies both caps (character cap on the real encoded length). checks.fix: Beta 1.195 GPS debug log toggle (PR #42): the 1.189/1.190 raw fix logger STAYS (Andrew reversed the same-day removal, PR #41, ten minutes after it merged; this build reverts it and converts the logger) behind a Settings switch in the Backup pane (#swFixLog). The enabled state is runtime-only: fixLogEnabled is a plain app3 let initialized false at every boot, with NO stored representation anywhere (not in SETTINGS/canonicalSettings, not in LS_GLOBAL, not in any backup field), reachable from app4 only through the doors fixLogIsEnabled/fixLogSetEnabled. Recording is gated at fixLogRaw (off = never recorded, storage never touched — fixLogClose's no-session early return keeps a logging-off watch stop from writing even an empty record); on mid-watch records from the next fix; off never deletes the log; segmentation stays by locate-on. Caps cut to ~1 hour: FIXLOG_MAX 3600, FIXLOG_MAX_CHARS 200000 (measured worst case ~46.0 chars/fix -> ~165,600 at 3,600, the rest margin). Proof: drive194 (39 checks, T1-T4 toggle sections + re-derived L sections). If a probe fails, the toggle has regressed or been reverted — restore the shipped form and re-run drive194.

checks.fix: Beta 1.198 camera glide (PR #45, merge 7a6cc3c5): both exponential camera chases in parts/app3.js are replaced by critically-damped springs (camSmoothDamp / camSmoothDampAngle, the SmoothDamp form) — bearing spring smoothTime 0.22 s on the wrapped angle (target theta + omega*h from heading filter 2a unchanged), centre spring smoothTime 0.32 s on the camera centre in world metres (target dispShownPos() unchanged). The 0.5 px / 0.3 deg deadbands are rest thresholds (error AND spring velocity ~0); the render parking tests gained camSpringsRest() beside dispSettled(); spring velocities zero whenever the follow is not the camera's owner. The correction cap is RELATIVE: maxStep = (20 + lastFixSpd) * dt, lastFixSpd refreshed in acceptFix past every refusal return from the accepted fix's own Doppler speed (Codex P2 round 2: an absolute cap cannot track above 72 km/h — ~600 m behind in a minute at 30 m/s; the relative form tracks a steady 30 m/s at a bounded 9.4 m lag, and at rest it is exactly the studied 20 m/s). An explicit re-centre is exempt from the cap until the return closes under 25 m (camUncapped, set by resumeFollow; Codex P2 round 1: a capped 1 km re-centre crawls ~50 s; measured exempt return reaches under 1 m in 1.6 s from 100 m / 2.0 s from 1 km, zero overshoot). Acceptance on the session-2 replay through the shipped code: worst bearing step 10.18 -> 4.50 deg, smoothed centre jerk p95 1,021 -> 191 m/s^3, worst camera excess over the vehicle's own speed exactly 20.00 m/s, corner error vs theta at parity (11.11 vs 10.97 mean), centre lag 323 ms median stated. Proof: PR #45 gate all four contexts success (Tier B set 20/20 incl. drive163 15/15 and drive194 39/39), camera drives locally green (148 42/42, 126 15/15, 197 27/27, 195 15/15, 168 8/8), Codex zero findings on the final head 378ac2c2 after two adjudicated REAL P2 fixes. If a probe fails, the glide has regressed or been reverted — restore the shipped form and re-run the camera drives.

The correction cap is RELATIVE: maxStep = (20 + lastFixSpd) * dt, lastFixSpd refreshed in acceptFix past every refusal return from the accepted fix's own Doppler speed (Codex P2 round 2: an absolute cap cannot track above 72 km/h — ~600 m behind in a minute at 30 m/s; the relative form tracks a steady 30 m/s at a bounded 9.4 m lag, and at rest it is exactly the studied 20 m/s). An explicit re-centre is exempt from the cap until the return closes under 25 m (camUncapped, set by resumeFollow; Codex P2 round 1: a capped 1 km re-centre crawls ~50 s; measured exempt return reaches under 1 m in 1.6 s from 100 m / 2.0 s from 1 km, zero overshoot). Acceptance on the session-2 replay through the shipped code: worst bearing step 10.18 -> 4.50 deg, smoothed centre jerk p95 1,021 -> 191 m/s^3, worst camera excess over the vehicle's own speed exactly 20.00 m/s, corner error vs theta at parity (11.11 vs 10.97 mean), centre lag 323 ms median stated. Proof: PR #45 gate all four contexts success (Tier B set 20/20 incl. drive163 15/15 and drive194 39/39), camera drives locally green (148 42/42, 126 15/15, 197 27/27, 195 15/15, 168 8/8), Codex zero findings on the final head 378ac2c2 after two adjudicated REAL P2 fixes. checks.fix: Beta 1.204 road snap, display-only (PR #51, merge 15dcfd272bdfc5d3b73ba58eb4282f3534cca24e; built and proven as Beta 1.197 on the 1.196 base, re-applied by hand onto dc70a295 and renumbered at landing - 1.201/1.202/1.203 shipped while it queued, and the in-app update check refuses a served version lower than the running one). WHAT IT IS: the map-matching study's gated continuity-hold matcher as an explicit driving state in parts/app3.js, a second presentation transform inside dispShownPos beside the 1.194 stillness hold - engage at >= 4 m/s with a candidate within 12 m (accuracy <= 20 m), a rival takes the hold only by beating it >= 3 m on 3 consecutive fixes, drop at > 18 m, evidence timeout (5 fixes > 10 m) with re-entry hysteresis (snapReject: the timed-out road cannot be re-taken by any path while fixes land past SNAP_FAR_M from it), release on one fix below 4 m/s, engage/release/switch all blend over ~0.8 s with no teleport (snapTakeHold anchors the blend on every road change and seeds snapSegHint from snapNearest's own segment; snapDropHold's blend-out capture is weight-normalized). DISPLAY-ONLY throughout: coverage, trail, distance banking and the fix logger read true positions only; Start Clean is a hard exit (snapReset is startClean's first statement; snapFix gates on runStart for the whole clean). Road data = the active route's lines + the shipped city pack for the fix's city via the app's own loader; no candidate nearby is always answered with the true position. THE GATE: seven rounds. Codex raised 7 findings across rounds 1-5, ALL REAL, all fixed in-round with drive200 pins: the drive's ENOENT fixture path (P1, round 1), the dead release blend-out (P2), the windowed projection accepting a far local minimum from hint 0 - reproduced offline at 813.6 m on Woodland Acres Crescent (P1), the full-blend switch teleport (P2), the double-weighted partial release capture (P2), the accuracy gate missing on drop-and-reengage (P2), and the evidence-timeout re-take loop in the 10-12 m band (P2). Rounds 6-7 were Codex-clean; round 6's checks failed on two TEST defects, both classified with evidence and re-derived in the drives with their bases written in: drive148 S3 (its premise expired - the camera now follows the snapped point; S3 grades the camera against the shown point's own stretch + 200 ms) and drive200's own determinism (settleIndex before every replay - an unsettled async pack install made A2 score 495/504 with a 9-fix wrong lock vs 537/537 settled; stepFeed synthetic feeds; C3 compares trail positions because trail points carry page-clock stamps). PROOF (gate run 43697597574, head 17844a67): plan, build-and-test, offline-e2e, all 8 shards and the tier-drives aggregator SUCCESS; codex bridge SUCCESS (43697595999); name-checked in shard logs: drive200 29/29 (shard 4), drive197 27/27 (shard 7), drive148 42/42 and drive194 39/39 (shard 3). Acceptance on the merged tree: S1 162/162 engaged within 3.5 m = 1.00000 (study bar 0.98148), S2 537/537 = 1.00000 (bar 0.99069), longest wrong-road locks 1 and 2 (bar <= 3), zero sub-gate engagements, phase B hard exit at the tap with recording normal during the clean, phase C logger rows byte-identical and trail positions/banked distance/coverage identical snapped vs unsnapped. Merged tree == tested head tree (be523121); live read-back: the served page is byte-identical (sha256) to the merged build, reads Beta 1.204 and contains the snap code. Roster 80 drives / 1377 checks. If a probe fails, the snap's state machine, its display-only invariant or its acceptance drive has regressed - restore the shipped form and re-run drive200 + drive197 + drive194.

Pack cache round (PR #70, merge a417427db94fa9fc45438a0de3d09a24f308e717; rollback: revert the merge -> 6ddbb380). Andrew approved 'fix all of it' in chat 2026-11-15, covering two assessed Carbon-sweep leftovers (human assessment: denylist-mediums-assessment; both graded REAL at LOW; the tile cache holds re-downloadable map data only, no stored format touched). C-02 (parts/app4.js, stDel): the offline-cache delete ran guarded only by the per-page preloadRunning flag, breaking the pack writers'-turn contract (takePackWriteTurn) both other pack mutations honour; it now acquires the turn and holds it across the delete and the metadata clears, released in a finally. C-01 (same file, the xPre download handler): downloads only ever PUT manifest URLs and never pruned entries orphaned by route deletions/updates (deleteRoute never touches the pack cache), so orphans survived every same-session download while the census weighed their bytes against the 250 MB cap; the download now prunes off-manifest entries (URL-normalized comparison, like migratePack) right after its census, subtracting the freed bytes from the cap accounting. Three Codex P2s in the PR #69/#70 gate hardened the prune before it shipped: the handler refreshes persisted route registrations (initUserPacks) before building the manifest; the prune runs only on a PROVEN manifest - a fresh full store read (upGetAll) succeeds and every persisted route, normalized via normalizePack, has its whole packTileUrls set inside the manifest (a content proof, not an ID check, so a route recreated under a reused ID in a different area fails it); and the pack turn is acquired FIRST, with the refresh and manifest built inside it, so a preceding writer's completed download cannot be overtaken by a stale snapshot. On any doubt the cache is preserved whole. Proofs: tests/proof/proof-pack-cache-c01.mjs (four scenarios, both-ways demonstrated at every gate step) and proof-pack-cache-c02.mjs. Maintenance, no Beta bump (page still reads Beta 1.205, live-verified byte-identical).

E-02: the prefers-reduced-motion block's selectors lost on specificity to the .boot/.open/.bye/.boot.show state rules (a media query adds none), so both full-screen menus still animated for reduced-motion users; the state selectors now ride inside the media block. E-05: #rmClose/#setClose/#setVer were absolute inside the scrolling menus and rode the content on short screens; they are fixed now, same resting spot. E-06: #selPop button (1,0,1) beat #selNote (1,0,0), squeezing the note icon into a 16px content box, and .selActs' min-content floor overflowed the card, pushing Clear off its edge; the note rule is re-scoped #selPop #selNote and the row is tightened until it fits. A second gate catch (drive128 M7b, APP): the restored 40px note height broke the Beta 1.34 one-size card invariant by 4px in the single-section state; .selActs now reserves min-height 40px in both states. Proof: tests/proof/proof-rerun-css-batch.mjs measures each failure property in the rendered app (8/36 baseline on unmodified main with the assessment's own numbers; 42/42 with the fixes, the last two checks being the gate catches demonstrated both ways). Gate: checks run 43749861586 SUCCESS (drive128 18/18 name-checked in shard 8), Codex zero findings on the final head, live page byte-identical to the merged build.

checks.fix: Re-run candidate D-04 fix (PR #77, merge d7c261403c651eef9386087fd1571ea3ce7e5a03; supersedes PR #75, closed unmerged after main moved via PR #76 while #75 sat fully green in its gate; rollback: revert the merge -> ec82d62e). From the 2026-11-15 Carbon sweep re-run candidates assessment (human assessment: rerun-candidates-assessment; graded REAL at LOW). Defect: crStreetParts in parts/create-pick.js computed a street's cut pieces against whatever city extract (crCov) existed at first view and cached the record in draft.parts permanently - coverage grows cell-by-cell inside one draft (grid cells, fallback box, top-up merges, cache fold) and nothing invalidated the cache, so opening a street's trim view before its area's extract landed froze it as one whole uncut piece for the rest of the draft; saved geometry was never wrong, the street just could not be trimmed finer than the stale record allowed. Fix: every record is stamped via crCovStamp() (extract generation + verified-box count + indexed-way count; every landing grows a count, a replacement extract bumps crCovGen) and an unreferenced record recomputes when the stamp has moved. Two Codex P2s in the PR #75 gate, both adjudicated REAL and cured in this tree, set the pin boundary: a record may be replaced only when nothing live references its pieces - a stored trim (draft.sectors indexes) or an open sector session for the street (its Cancel snapshot, sector bar, and the rendered draft features whose sector indexes crSectorTap reads; coverage landings verified not to redraw the draft) pins it, and the recompute lands at the next read after the reference clears (crOpenSectors settles the record before a session's first render). Proof: tests/proof/proof-rerun-d04-streetparts-covstamp.mjs, 15 checks - fails on unmodified main (5), on the PR #75 first head at S5 (snapshot), on the remedy-1 head at S6 (session stability), passes 15/15 shipped. Sibling caches audited and left: crDraftGeom/crGeomCache (draft-geometry inputs only), crPending (re-resolved by crSweepPending on landing), draft.roads (user state). Foreign-write census re-pinned on line count alone (create-pick.js followPaused 660 -> 683; totals unchanged, 57 expressions / 24 lines). Maintenance, no Beta bump (page still reads Beta 1.205, live-verified byte-identical to the merged build).

Sweep re-run B-05 fix (PR #78, merge 90d90fdc7f1b08094abc9b8c3e83433365e9e2c4; fresh copy of Carbon sweep PR #73, closed unmerged as superseded after main moved under it three times - #73 had passed its gate but branch protection requires an up-to-date branch; rollback: revert the merge -> d7c26140). From the 2026-11-15 Carbon sweep re-run (sweep-20261115-171048, finding B-05, graded MEDIUM by Carbon; the fix is Carbon's own, carried byte-identical). Defect: GLP.init in parts/engine.js rebuilt the engine's data only when CUR was null (`if (!CUR) { rebuildData(); lastSig = stateSig(); }`), so if the map layer dropped (GLP.drop) and state changed while it was down - a selection made or cleared, pieces marked - a later init() on a fresh map pushed the stale CUR via addStack and the changes never showed; stateSig() covers pieces only, so selection changes were invisible to the sig mechanism too. Fix: init() re-derives sel from the host's selStretch, rebuilds when CUR is null OR stateSig() has moved since lastSig, and otherwise refreshes only the selection layers (buildSelC/buildSel). Proof: tests/proof/proof-sweep-20261115-171048-b-05.mjs (the sweep's own proof, unchanged) - fails on unmodified main (Check 1: sel source 0 features after re-init, expected 1), passes 3/3 shipped (verified both ways again in the PR #78 round on a fresh clone at d7c26140). Maintenance, no Beta bump (live page byte-identical to the merged build, sha256 ed2a49f1..., still reads Beta 1.205).

Denylist fix round (PR #79, merge 8343246d0cd01e94437e13e947cb2fdae5f21833; rollback: revert the merge -> 90d90fdc). From the 2026-11-15 Carbon sweep re-run denylist assessment (finding A-05, graded REAL, LOW; Andrew approved fixing the 2 real ones). Defect: loadRouteState's history sanitizer stripped streets absent from the current pack in place, and saveHistory / saveAll / finishRun's archive write then persisted the stripped view - a load-time strip became a permanent write, contradicting the codebase's own rule (dropPhantom: a load-time strip is a view, never a write). Fix: the sanitizer runs as one indexed pass (same predicates, same view) recording a snapshot (histRawList / histRawView); the four writers persist historyForWrite(...) so strip-dropped raw entries ride back verbatim, survivors are written in raw form, user deletions still delete, finishes still append; dropPhantom pops the snapshot in step; unloadRouteToBoot clears it via resetHistorySnapshot(). No stored-data format change. (Re-pinned 2026-11-22 by arch2-1272, Beta 1.272, architecture programme #2: the guarded code moved into the HIST history repository; the invariant is unchanged.)

Street-end width fix (Beta 1.206, PR #81, merge 22ab3ea217a733b012e674ec376422c9acfeebb4; rollback: revert the merge -> 8343246d). Defect (Andrew-reported 2026-11-15; investigation street-end-gaps/RECORD.md): at close zoom the drawn paint width shrank below the geographic design width (MapLibre interpolation + the zoom-19 pixel cap), leaving ~1.9 m (z17) / ~2.5 m (z18) / ~3.0 m (z19) of bare asphalt where a street's paint ends at a crossing street, while every end's geometry was already flush-cut at the crossing paint edge. Fix (parts/engine.js width stops only, ZERO geometry change - mergeStrands-protocol canonical hashes identical on all states incl. one/velmar0/velmar1/greenpark0, the green-line run-through guarantee): surfW z16-19 raised so the surface draws its 9.90 m design width at z16-19 (z14 stop untouched); BANDW draws ~14.4 m from z15; BANDCASE follows BANDW + the shipped rim, with the z15 stop RULED 8.04 (the candidate clone's 10.8 had no derivation and contradicted the spec; 8.04 = BANDW 5.54 + the shipped z15 rim 2.5); t1-casing stops re-derived so the surface casing rim is identical to shipped at every stop. Companion defect caught by the gate (Codex P2 on PR #81, real, fixed in-round): the click handler's fixed 24 px tap tolerance (the Beta 1.181 value chosen so a tap anywhere on the paint selects) no longer covered the widened paint at z18-19 (band+casing half-width 37 px / 71 px); tolerance now GLP.tapTolPx(z) = max(24, BANDCASE(z)/2 + 2) in engine.js, read by the handler in parts/app2.js - 24 px unchanged at z17 and below, 39 px at z18, 73.1 px at z19. Proof: tests/proof/proof-street-end-width-fix.mjs (8 checks incl. the tap-tolerance check) - ALL PASS on the shipped tree, 19 failures on unmodified main; wired into CI build-and-test. Gate: run 43765803912 SUCCESS (plan, build-and-test, offline-e2e, all 8 shards, tier drives); Codex zero findings on final head 4d8af744; merged tree blob-identical to the tested tree; live page byte-identical to the merged build (sha256 300119a1...), reads Beta 1.206. Gate round 1 failures classified: drive194 L1 TEST (live-version pin rolled 1.205 -> 1.206, the standing per-bump roll) and drive180 NOTILE2 FLAKE (splash-pixel; prior flakes PRs #56/#67/#75; passed on the re-run). Design QA on the rendered fixed build: drawn surface 9.86-9.87 m at z16-19 (shipped 8.41/6.14/4.85/3.88), band 14.3-14.4 m z15-19, casing rims == shipped, day+night screenshots at Kingsnorth x Santa Barbara and Greenpark x Valeria show terminating paint meeting crossing paint. Companion defect caught by the gate (Codex P2 on PR #81, real, fixed in-round): the click handler's fixed 24 px tap tolerance (the Beta 1.181 value chosen so a tap anywhere on the paint selects) no longer covered the widened paint at z18-19 (band+casing half-width 37 px / 71 px); tolerance now GLP.tapTolPx(z) = max(24, BANDCASE(z)/2 + 2) in engine.js, read by the handler in parts/app2.js - 24 px unchanged at z17 and below, 39 px at z18, 73.1 px at z19. Proof: tests/proof/proof-street-end-width-fix.mjs (8 checks incl. the tap-tolerance check) - ALL PASS on the shipped tree, 19 failures on unmodified main; wired into CI build-and-test. Gate: run 43765803912 SUCCESS (plan, build-and-test, offline-e2e, all 8 shards, tier drives); Codex zero findings on final head 4d8af744; merged tree blob-identical to the tested tree; live page byte-identical to the merged build (sha256 300119a1...), reads Beta 1.206. Gate round 1 failures classified: drive194 L1 TEST (live-version pin rolled 1.205 -> 1.206, the standing per-bump roll) and drive180 NOTILE2 FLAKE (splash-pixel; prior flakes PRs #56/#67/#75; passed on the re-run). Design QA on the rendered fixed build: drawn surface 9.86-9.87 m at z16-19 (shipped 8.41/6.14/4.85/3.88), band 14.3-14.4 m z15-19, casing rims == shipped, day+night screenshots at Kingsnorth x Santa Barbara and Greenpark x Valeria show terminating paint meeting crossing paint. Out of scope, untouched: Topper x Mellings corner shortfall.

checks.fix: Beta 1.246 (PR #129, merge ba75ddbc; rollback: a revert PR restoring the 1.245 behaviour under Beta 1.247). The stall round (Andrew's Apple-standard rule, locked 2026-11-18): a create-flow street-data download that goes completely silent gives up that ONE attempt after 60 s instead of hanging. The rule lands INSIDE crOverpassFetch (parts/create-fetch.js) as a per-attempt silence timer (CR_TIMING.attemptStallMs 60000): armed at the attempt's start, re-armed when the answer lands and on every streamed chunk, aborting the attempt through its own controller so the loop gives the next instance the budget that remains; one shared clearTimers retires it with the cap timer at every exit. A trickling download re-arms per chunk and is never cut by it. The preparation watchdogs' stallMs DELIBERATELY stays 180000: they measure silence in landings, not bytes, and at 60000 they would cut fetches the 120 s budget would have let live (a fallback prep is one fetch - an honest 90 s answer would be failed and orphaned at 60), breaking the rule's own slow-but-alive clause; proof-1246 checks 4/8/9 pin the adjudication. Gate: plan, build-and-test, tier drives and the codex review gate all SUCCESS on head c89fed91 (checks.yml changed, so the full 8-shard battery ran; Codex clean receipt on that head, has_any_findings false); merged tree == tested tree (26690a25); live page byte-identical to the merged build (sha256 24d6cd6e, #ver Beta 1.246). Proof: tests/proof/proof-1246.mjs (11 checks; 7 fail on pristine 1.245 - the 4 passes pin what must not change); tests/browser/drive205.mjs (7 checks: silent attempt killed at 3110 ms scaled / the fallback commits; a ~9.6 s trickle completes from the first instance; a killed attempt's late poison changes nothing; a wedged no-stream text() cut at the bound; the healthy path identical - on pristine the timing sections run to the 20000 ms cap and fail). The shipped 60 s bound was also run once at real time locally: kill at 60001 ms, fallback committed. If a probe here fails, the round has regressed - restore the shipped form.

Andrew's approved design of 2026-11-21 for the cold-start name blink (diagnosis cold-start-flicker-2026-11-21: the one-flight hook's re-place tears labelpts down at the flight's idle and all 33 titles vanish for the re-parse exactly as the basemap names finish fading in): on a route pick, every name is held out for the whole load-in window, the re-place runs inside the hold, and at the settled idle all names fade in together over one 350 ms ramp, with backstop reveals (6 s post-re-place; an absolute 15 s). The hold is two kinds: title layers by a multiplier that TRANSFORMS their text-opacity (scaleNameStops rebuilds a zoom interpolate/step with scaled outputs - the paint validator silently refuses any value embedding the layer's own expression, measured), basemap name layers by VISIBILITY ONLY (nameHoldHideOnly - a single text-opacity write on a basemap symbol layer resets its tiles' placement state and blanks a marginal title at the next zoom boundary, measured: Bell Harbour, drive216 P3). Every held layer leaves placement (visibility 'none') while the window stands; natural paint and visibility are captured on first touch and restored verbatim at the ramp's end. app5 owns the cycle (beginNameLoadIn and family, generation-counted per pick; the hook gains a 6.5 s arm-time backstop). The create backdrop coordinates through nameHoldNaturalVis/nameBackdropHolds and a record top-up (PR #162 Codex). drive219 grades the rendered behaviour (15/15; fails 9-10 of 14 on the 1.265 tree, its lane convicting the blink by name in the denser runs); proof-1266 pins the shape statically (12/12, mutations observed for the wrap, the backstop, the paint ban and the backdrop consult). If a probe here fails, the round has regressed - restore the shipped form. RE-PINNED 2026-11-24 by the label round (Beta 1.290): the machinery this probe pinned was deleted whole by approved design (geometry-anchored titles); the probe now asserts the deletion holds.

The runner now owns the reap: per-drive TMPDIR on the home disk removed at drive close, a post-drive reap of residue created during the drive, and a startup sweep of residue older than an hour. Verified live 2026-11-22: drive204 25/25 through the edited runner with zero new /tmp residue; the runner/cleanup self-test fixture failures are environmental (identical on the pristine runner - known-env-failures.md). (Revised 2026-11-22, Beta 1.272, Codex P2 on PR #168: the name+timestamp sweep of shared /tmp could delete another live drive's profile - the sweep is GONE. The runner now gives each drive its own TMPDIR under this base, removed at drive close, and the harness + create rigs build profiles under TMPDIR. The probe follows the owned-dir mechanism.)
